title: Authentic Aromatic Middle Eastern Lentils Mujadara
description: A traditional Middle Eastern dish made with lentils and rice, infused with aromatic spices and topped with caramelized onions, this recipe is a hearty and flavorful weeknight meal option, featuring egg white and wood-fired bake elements, while being ayurvedic-sattvic-friendly.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit for wood-fired baking effect.
In a large pot, combine the lentils and water, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
In a large bowl, combine the cooked lentils, rice, salt, black pepper, cumin, and coriander, and mix well.
In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat, and cook the sliced onions for 20 minutes, or until caramelized.
In a small bowl, whisk the egg white until stiff peaks form, and set aside.
In a large baking dish, combine the lentil and rice mixture, and top with the caramelized onions and whisked egg white.
Bake the mujadara in the preheated oven for 20 minutes, or until the egg white is set and the onions are golden brown.
Remove the mujadara from the oven, and let it cool for 10 minutes before serving.
